The AI calendar is stacked with bullish catalysts — Meta Connect, OpenAI DevDay, and Micron earnings — creating a potential re-rating moment for the sector. Meta's Muse AI agent is seeing surging downloads, Shopify integration is live, and investor sentiment is building ahead of the keynote. AutoZone's management flagged positive sales linearity, and travel, housing, and consumer staples names are all showing relative strength.
bear_case: Financials are getting hit broadly — banks, brokers, insurers, and asset managers are all underperforming — suggesting rotation out of economically sensitive and rate-sensitive names. CMS lab service rate cuts hit Quest Diagnostics and Lab Corp harder than anticipated, a reminder that regulatory pricing risk is real across healthcare. Texas Governor Abbott has now blocked both power grid connections and new permitting for data centers, adding a meaningful headwind to the data center buildout narrative. SB Energy delayed its IPO after investors pushed back on its $50 billion-plus valuation, signaling sentiment on the data center boom may be cooling at the margin.

company_items.summary: AutoZone reported fiscal Q4 EPS of $56.05 versus the Street's $54.03, but the beat was low quality — tariff refunds added 145 basis points to gross margins and a non-cash LIFO impact added another 105 basis points. Domestic comps of plus 1.6% missed the Street's plus 3.1% estimate, and the operating expense ratio worsened 100 basis points year-over-year. Management noted positive comp linearity in the quarter, which is helping the stock hold gains despite the quality concerns.

MillerKnoll reported solid fiscal Q1 EPS of 53 cents versus the Street's 36 cents, and importantly the beat was real — even excluding an 11-cent tariff refund tailwind, EPS would have been 42 cents, still well ahead of consensus. Guidance is mixed, with fiscal 2027 sales range trimmed but the EPS outlook left unchanged.

THOR Industries missed fiscal Q4 EPS at 78 cents versus the Street's 87 cents, with gross margins falling 230 basis points year-over-year to 12.4% versus the Street's 13.85% estimate. Revenue came in at $2.311 billion, down 8.4% year-over-year but slightly above the Street's $2.17 billion estimate. Management cited a difficult macro landscape.

Meta's Muse personal AI agent is seeing surging downloads ahead of Zuckerberg's Connect keynote Wednesday night, with investor expectations turning increasingly bullish. Shopify confirmed it will allow Muse to complete purchases on its e-commerce platform, a meaningful distribution win, though Amazon has blocked Muse from its platform. OpenAI is reportedly developing a competing product, underscoring the competitive urgency in the agentic AI race.

Shopify announced it will allow Meta's Muse AI agent to complete purchases on its e-commerce platform, positioning itself as a key partner in the agentic commerce ecosystem. This follows Amazon's decision to block Muse, which could drive incremental transaction volume toward Shopify merchants.

Quest Diagnostics shares were hit Tuesday after CMS released new Medicare payment rates for lab services that represented a larger-than-anticipated reduction. The rate cuts also pressured Lab Corp, suggesting a sector-wide negative pricing event rather than a company-specific issue.

Lab Corp shares fell alongside Quest Diagnostics after CMS issued new Medicare lab service payment rates with cuts larger than the market had expected. The across-the-board pressure on lab testing names signals a meaningful regulatory pricing headwind for the sector.

Cognex announced it will acquire RealSense, described as the market leader in depth-sensing cameras and vision technology for robotic perception and Physical AI, for approximately $500 million upfront plus an additional $106.5 million. The deal positions Cognex more aggressively in the Physical AI and robotics supply chain at a time of growing industry interest in the space.

Viking Therapeutics reported positive trial results for its GLP-1 drug VK2735, including 22% weight loss in trial participants. This keeps Viking competitive in the increasingly crowded obesity drug space and validates the asset's commercial potential.

Alibaba unveiled what it described as China's most powerful AI chip and hinted at plans to train a model with up to 10 trillion parameters, while management outlined plans to operate more than 20 gigawatts of data center capacity by 2032. The announcement reinforces Alibaba's ambition to compete at the frontier of AI infrastructure and model development.
